200g Powdered Sugar to Cups Converter

Convert 200 grams of powdered (confectioners) sugar into standard US baking cups for perfect frostings and glazes.

Cup Equivalent:

Roughly 1 2/3 cups (1.67 cups)

*Calculated using standard US customary culinary measuring cups for unsifted powdered sugar.

Converting 200 Grams of Powdered Sugar to Cups

200 grams of powdered sugar is the gold standard for a full batch of American buttercream frosting — enough to generously frost a two-layer 8-inch cake or 24 cupcakes. At 120 grams per unsifted cup, 200 grams converts to roughly 1.67 cups, or about 1 2/3 cups. This is nearly double the volume you would get from 200g of granulated sugar, which is why frosting recipes can seem voluminous.

The Mathematical Conversion Formula

Divide the given mass by the standard weight of powdered sugar per cup:

  • Total Cup Volume = Given Weight in Grams ÷ Standard Powdered Sugar Weight Per Cup
  • Powdered: 200g ÷ 120g/cup = 1.67 cups (roughly 1 2/3 cups)
  • Granulated: 200g ÷ 200g/cup = 1.00 cup (exactly 1 cup)
  • Packed Brown: 200g ÷ 220g/cup = 0.91 cups (just under 1 cup)

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: How many cups is 200g of powdered sugar?

A1: 200 grams of powdered sugar equals roughly 1.67 cups, or about 1 2/3 cups. This is the standard amount for a full batch of buttercream frosting.

Q2: Why does 200g of powdered sugar look like so much in the bowl?

A2: Powdered sugar is very light and airy. At only 120g per cup, 200g expands to over 1 2/3 cups in volume. The fine particles trap air, making it appear much larger in volume than the same weight of denser sugars like brown or granulated.

Q3: How do I avoid a powdered sugar cloud when measuring 200g?

A3: To minimize mess, spoon powdered sugar gently into the measuring cup rather than scooping directly from the bag. Better yet, weigh 200g directly on a digital kitchen scale in the mixing bowl to avoid any mess entirely.
